title: HAAN: A Holistic Approach for Accelerating Normalization Operations in Large Language Models
problem: Normalization operations (LayerNorm) in LLMs substantially elevate processing latency and energy consumption, becoming a performance bottleneck.
motivation: LayerNorm is ubiquitous across all LLM layers for training stability and convergence; optimizing it yields significant system-level performance gains.
method: HAAN tackles the normalization bottleneck—the step where models stabilize values flowing through the network—by jointly redesigning the computation and the hardware that runs it. Rather than keeping the algorithm fixed and hoping hardware will improve, the approach tweaks the computation itself and designs specialized hardware tailored to run that exact algorithm. This co-design (joint optimization of algorithm and hardware) reduces both latency and energy consumption. Because normalization happens frequently in LLM inference, even small per-operation gains compound into significant overall speedups.
key_novelty: The core idea is applying co-design (joint algorithm-and-hardware optimization) to normalization in LLM inference.
contributions: Significantly better hardware performance than state-of-the-art solutions
limitations: Specific performance metrics and speedup numbers not detailed in abstract.
